Found and fixed a CRITICAL bug invisible to every prior curl-based verification this session: mock-wawu-id had no CORS headers, so the real browser auth handshake was silently falling back to a FAKE mock-token session (auth.ts's own resilience pattern masked it) -- every subsequent Hub API call would have 401'd in real use. This is the concrete case for why Phase 8 is mandatory rather than 'the API contracts check out' -- see WAWU-Hub-API commit db4b347.

Also fixed live: WAWU-Web's shared Input component had no label/input id association at all when no id/name prop was passed (broke accessibility AND getByLabel-style testing) -- see WAWU-Web commit 6b1c4a8.

Verified a full write-path round trip (join community -> send message -> real POST -> re-render with new message + real credit decrement). Verified the full new-user sign-up flow end-to-end: real WAWU-ID register -> real Hub onboarding PATCH -> real OTP verify -> real home feed landing, for an identity that did not exist before the run.

New gap found live (not previously known): SSR/CSR hydration mismatch on every authenticated page load (AppShell/Sidebar/DesktopHeader render without session server-side, then re-render with it client-side) -- recoverable, not a crash, but a real architecture gap from adding localStorage persistence in Phase 6 without SSR-awareness in the shell components. Flagged, not fixed this session (non-trivial, needs a mounted-state guard or disabling SSR on these shells).

SearchResponse: recentSearches always returns [] -- no per-user search-history table in the frozen schema. Known gap, not silently hidden.
SearchResponse: /search/closest uses tokenized ILIKE, not real fuzzy/trigram matching -- pg_trgm is not enabled in any migration and enabling it is a schema change out of this resource's scope.

Community: private-community join creates a real status=pending CommunityMembership row, but the frontend has no UI for that pending state at all (ui-align-tasks.json) -- a Phase-6 task, not a backend gap.

CommunityMessage: no product-owner confirmation that the community host should be subject to the same credit gate as any other member when posting in their own community -- built literally per the frozen contract (no exemption specified), flagged for a real decision.

SYSTEMIC (Phase 6 finding, highest priority): no resource that returns a bare wawuId (ContentPiece.creatorWawuId, DirectMessage.creatorWawuId/senderWawuId, CommunityMessage.senderWawuId, Community.hostWawuId) joins a display name/handle/avatar. Every affected frontend surface falls back to the raw id or a generic placeholder ('Creator'/'Buyer') rather than a real name. Needs either a batch profile-lookup endpoint or per-resource joins.

PRODUCT DECISION NEEDED: the designed OTP screen (design/screens/WAWU Auth.dc.html) collects and displays an EMAIL address, but WAWU ID's only OTP capability (POST /auth/otp/verify) is phone-based, WhatsApp-delivered -- there is no email-OTP endpoint anywhere. Frontend now wired to the real phone-based flow (src/types/auth.ts's OtpVerifyPayload), but the screen's copy still says 'email' and WAWU-ID's register() endpoint issues tokens immediately with no OTP step ever actually triggered in the current sign-up flow. Needs a product decision: drop the OTP step for email/password signup, or rebuild it around phone/WhatsApp.

No Flutterwave inline-checkout SDK wired into the frontend anywhere yet. Every payment-shaped flow (content unlock, tips, DM send, CAC application, credits purchase, subscribe/upgrade) uses a synthetic-transaction-id-then-verify bridge against the backend's MockFlutterwaveAdapter, matching the pre-existing content-unlock pattern. Works end-to-end locally against the mock adapter; will NOT represent a real charge once a real Flutterwave key is configured -- a real checkout-widget integration is required before any payment flow can go live.

FollowRelationship has no GET (am-I-following) endpoint; Community has no leave/unjoin endpoint; SavedItem's list returns bare rows with no embedded ContentPiece (frontend enriches client-side via a follow-up getContent() call per row, currently returns [] live because ContentPiece responses themselves lack a creator object -- see the systemic gap above); GET /users/:wawuId/public-profile has no fullName/location/verificationLevel/dmEnabled/dmPrice fields, only counts.
GET /explore/creators (creator discovery/listing) has no real backend endpoint at all -- stays mock-only, cannot be substituted by /search (requires non-empty free-text q).

Local dev port collision risk: WAWU ID's main.ts and Next.js's `next dev` both default to port 3000. Phase 8 avoided this by pointing NEXT_PUBLIC_WAWU_ID_BASE_URL at mock-wawu-id (:4001) instead of the real WAWU ID -- still relevant whenever someone runs the real WAWU ID service locally alongside this frontend.

NEW (found live in Phase 8, not previously known): SSR/CSR hydration mismatch on every authenticated page load -- AppShell/Sidebar/DesktopHeader/FocusedFlowShell render without session server-side (localStorage doesn't exist during SSR) then re-render with the real session client-side. Recoverable (React discards+replaces, no crash) but causes a visible flash and will look like an error in dev mode. Needs a mounted-state guard (or SSR disabled) on these shell components -- not fixed this session, flagged for a dedicated follow-up.

The real, separately-deployed WAWU ID service was never exercised in this entire session (no credentials/DB available in this sandbox) -- mock-wawu-id stood in throughout, built to match the real contract by direct code inspection. This is the single largest remaining live-connectivity risk before any real deployment.

No real Flutterwave key/connectivity was exercised anywhere this session -- every payment flow verified only against MockFlutterwaveAdapter. A real inline-checkout SDK integration on the frontend (currently a synthetic-transaction bridge) is required before any payment flow can go live, in addition to real Flutterwave credentials.
